wormald.wormald_origin: English copy of a Carolingian (Frankish) manual; Wormald rejects Conner's case for an Exeter origin, but holds that it or its exemplar was within reach of the makers of the Worcester collections (Nero A.i, CCCC 265, CCCC 190) (p. 223 n. 240; p. 218 n. 217).
wormald.other_contents: A Carolingian manual of penitential and canon law: Ecgberht's penitential with Ghaerbald of Liège's capitulary inserted between its preface and body; its last and largest item is the Carolingian canon-law handbook called Quadripartitus (pp. 216, 218); the same arrangement passed into three English pontificals (p. 216).
wormald.overview: Bodley 718 is an English copy, made in the mid-tenth century, of a Frankish handbook of penance and church law; it contains no Anglo-Saxon laws. Wormald sees the arrangement of its continental model, in which Ghaerbald of Liège's capitulary sits inside Ecgberht's penitential, as the root of the confusion behind the so-called Excerptiones Ecgberhti, and notes that its final item, the Carolingian canon collection known as Quadripartitus, was among the chief sources of those Excerpts. He doubts the case for an Exeter origin but accepts that the book or its model was available to the compilers of the Worcester canon collections.
wormald.key_quote: Bodley 718, a mid-tenth-century English copy of a Carolingian manual of penitential and canon law (p. 216)
wormald.doubts: Not in the guide. Its 'Quadripartitus' is a Carolingian canon-law collection, not the twelfth-century English Quadripartitus of Liebermann's Q — beware confusion. Context only.
verify_notes: Checked pp. 216–18, 223 (n. 240). Overview: 'major source of the Wulfstan canon collection' overstated — Wormald says the Carolingian Quadripartitus (its last item) was a major source of the Excerptiones (p. 218), with close textual links (n. 216); rewritten, quotation marks removed, Exeter point added (n. 217, n. 240).
Pages: n. 211 (Hohler on the 'tangle' of Bodley 718's exemplar) added; key_quote verified p. 216.
